thread.title: Stocks - Nvidia, Facebook Slump in Pre-market; PG&E, Blackberry Rise

author: Investing.com
title: Stocks - Nvidia, Facebook Slump in Pre-market; PG&E, Blackberry Rise
text:
Investing.com - Stocks in focus in pre-market trade Friday:
· NVIDIA Corporation (NASDAQ:NVDA) stock plummeted 17% as of 8:20 AM ET (13:20 GMT) after the company missed on revenue and forecast a fall in chip sales for the holiday quarter as demand for Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL) products waned.
· Pacific Gas & Electric Co (NYSE:PCG) stock increased 46% after a report that the California Public Utilities Commission does not want the the company to go into bankruptcy should it be found responsible for the wildfire in northern California.
· Facebook (NASDAQ:FB) stock was down 1.25% amid pressure over how the social media network manages community standards and posts.
· Bank of America (NYSE:BAC) stock inched down 0.54% after news that the Justice Department has asked the bank for information about transactions they handled for an Estonian branch of Danske Bank, which is at the center of one of the biggest money-laundering investigations in history.
· BlackBerry (NYSE:BB) stock rose 2% after it announced it is acquiring artificial intelligence and cybersecurity company Cylance in a $1.4 billion cash deal.
· T-Mobile (NASDAQ:TMUS) stock fell 0.12% after its chief financial officer said its deal with Sprint could close in the first quarter of 2019.
· Applied Materials (NASDAQ:AMAT) stock tumbled 8%. While it beat earnings estimates, the chip company reported weak revenue and earnings guidance.
· Nordstrom (NYSE:JWN) stock slipped 12% following a miss in net profit. The retailer reported earnings of $0.39, including a one-time charge, missing estimates of $0.66, but reportined a revenue of $3.75 billion compared to expectations of $3.69 billion.
· Williams-Sonoma (NYSE:WSM) stock decreased 13% following results that missed on revenue.
· Sonos (NASDAQ:SONO) stock soared 18% after the electronics maker reported $272.9 million in revenue, beating estimates of $248.6 million.
· Viacom (NASDAQ:VIA) stock gained 3% after the company’s fourth-quarter earnings came in higher than expected.
